## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nānāchandajātaka* (Ja 289) is a canonical birth story found in the Jātaka collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya. The text opens with the canonical verse beginning *Nānacchandā mahārājā ti* ("Diverse are desires, great king") [Fausböll 1879]. According to its traditional frame story (*nidāna*), the Buddha related this account while dwelling at Jetavana concerning the Venerable Ānanda's reception of eight boons (*aṭṭhavaralābha*), noting that the fuller background narrative is elaborated in the *Juṇhajātaka* of the Eleventh Nipāta (*Ekādasanipāta*) [Fausböll 1879]. In the story of the past (*atītavatthu*), the Bodhisatta was reborn as the prince and heir to King Brahmadatta of Bārāṇasī, acquired arts and sciences at Takkasilā, and subsequently ascended the throne, during which time his father's deposed chaplain (*purohita*) lived in poverty in a dilapidated house [Fausböll 1879].

 Automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus indicates that segments from the canonical verse (§§1.1–2.4) correspond directly with the commentary in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Dutiyo bhāgo) as well as the later anthology *Nīti-gantha-saṅgaho Naradakkhadīpanī* [DharmaNexus].
